note: Round-4 gauntlet complete (FINAL, 21 warm-150 frozen-clock shots, all viewed; 0 console/module errors across ALL shots; every module reports 'live'). The six reworked modules show genuine quality gains, judged on pixels: terrain's coastline is now irregular (bays + headlands) with a water depth gradient + shore foam and cliff strata + vegetation — a real step up from R3's perfect disc, but from directly above the city is still a circular landmass/plate ringed by flat water on ALL sides, the single most visible remaining non-AAA element (g4f-terrain, g4f-city-aerial-day); environment's mountains gained a snowline + base vegetation and the day sky is de-milked/crisper, holding the already-strong dusk/night atmosphere (g4f-env-day, g4f-city-dusk); buildings added street-level detail (recessed ground floors, mullions, pilaster bays, canopy/balcony bands) on top of the already-strong dense lit skyline with spires (g4f-bldg-day, g4f-bldg-sky); traffic added real pedestrians on the sidewalks (capsule+head, denser near commercial) plus night car bodies with headlight/taillight pools (g4f-traffic-day, g4f-traffic-night); UI is the standout of the round — a real minimap (terrain height-shade, roads, camera frustum + north marker), a stats panel with icons/trend arrows/sparkline/services breakdown, and a notification toast, now genuinely close to CS2 (g4f-city-day); effects is now grounded (terrain ground + sea horizon, not a void) with a per-light bloom cap that keeps the glow tasteful (g4f-effects-night). Only UI and AUDIO clear the 8.5 pass bar. demoCity is 8.0 (dusk 8.5 / night 8.5 / day 8.0 / street 7.0, the street frame held down by a large low-poly tree blob in the foreground + boxy facades). The city is now strong good-indie leaning AAA on atmosphere + HUD; the terrain-plate, flat untextured road surface, soft low-poly mountain/tree silhouettes, and the near-empty simulation showcase are what still block a uniform AAA pass.

blindAB.method: knowledge-based CS2-calibrated A/B (no real CS2 frames in sandbox); whole-game holistic critic
tells: Circular floating landmass in flat water — from orbit/aerial the city is a disc of terrain ringed by flat, unreflected water on ALL sides; CS2 is a real coastal island whose landmass runs to the map border with a horizon sea and depth-varied, reflective water.

Flat untextured surfaces — roads are a flat dark slab (no asphalt texture, wear, curbs, or edge lines) and building facades are flat solid colors with grid windows (no PBR material, grime, glass reflection, or signage); the single most immediate 'not a real engine' tell at street range.

Low-poly props — a large smooth green tree-blob sits in the street-frame foreground and cars are boxy with no legible wheels/glass; CS2 street props are high-fidelity (leafy trees, real cars, benches/hydrants/signage).
Soft low-poly mountain silhouettes — the rim peaks are smooth and lack rock strata, ridgeline definition, and surface texture.

Sparse micro-detail + near-empty simulation 3D showcase — little rooftop clutter or street furniture, no service vehicles, and the isolated sim view renders a dark empty plain, so the 'living city' read depends almost entirely on the lit orbit frames.
blindAB.note: Strong good-indie leaning AAA: the dusk/night orbit atmosphere and the CS2-rich HUD (real minimap, stat icons/trends, toast) are genuinely top-tier, but the floating circular terrain plate and flat untextured roads/facades keep the composed city below the 8.5 AAA bar. Single highest-leverage fix: make it a real coastal city (land to the map border, sea at the edge, water reflections) to kill the floating-disc read.
